E-04.question: Q2 minimum investment plan for F&B (restaurant/cafe), incl. the reported IDR 10bn per KBLI per location rule  [DEAL-BREAKER vs CHF 200k frame]
E-04.question_or_metric: General rule: PMA total investment must exceed IDR 10bn excluding land and building, per 5-digit KBLI per project location. For food-and-beverage services (KBLI 56) the exception makes it IDR 10bn excluding land and building per 2-digit KBLI per one location point, where a location point means per kabupaten/kota. So the rule applies to restaurants and cafes; it is not a per-outlet rule but a per-city, per-KBLI-56-group rule (analysis: 56101 and 56303 would share one threshold in the same city). No single-outlet relief, phasing or reduced regime found in Art. 26-27.
E-04.value: lebih besar dari Rp10.000.000.000,00 (planned investment excl. land and building; F&B: per 2 digit KBLI per 1 titik lokasi = per kabupaten/kota)
E-04.unit: IDR total planned investment, excluding land and building; per 2-digit KBLI per city (F&B); general rule per 5-digit KBLI per project location
E-04.quote_or_snippet: [P2-A1A3-S1] total investasi lebih besar dari Rp10.000.000.000,00 (sepuluh miliar rupiah), di luar tanah dan bangunan per bidang usaha KBLI 5 (lima) digit per lokasi proyek || [P2-A1A3-S1] jasa makanan dan minuman, lebih besar dari Rp10.000.000.000,00 (sepuluh miliar rupiah) di luar tanah dan bangunan, adalah per 2 (dua) digit awal KBLI per 1 (satu) titik lokasi || [P2-A1A3-S1] Ketentuan Titik lokasi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (3) huruf b berlaku per kabupaten/kota
E-04.notes: Disconfirming detail for the plan: the F&B exception is per 2-digit KBLI (broader aggregation than per 5-digit), which favours multi-outlet roll-out within one city but does not lower the first-outlet threshold. Run 2 verification (2026-10-17): added text: Art. 364(3)(h) makes failure to meet the Art. 26 PMA investment limit a ground for administrative sanction in supervision ("tidak memenuhi batas ketentuan nilai investasi bagi PMA sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 26"), so the test is not only an OSS input check (sanction type not stated in the part read; Art. 365 refers to the types). Art. 28(3): in DKI Jakarta the authority of the kabupaten/kota DPMPTSP is exercised by the provincial government, which bears on the "kabupaten/kota" location point; the texts do not say whether an administrative city counts as kabupaten/kota (lawyer question Q1). Citation also adds Art. 26(1). The "per 2-digit KBLI = division 56" mapping of 56101 and 56303 is an inference (no provision lists the codes). "H1 refuted on the text" is the worker hypothesis verdict; see Q1-Q5 in tasks/2026-10-17-run2-verification-f.md for what could still reverse it. No SME, partnership, franchise or single-outlet relief found in Art. 26.
E-04.amendment_check: See E-08; no amendment found. Confirmed also at government-regulation level in PP 28/2025 Art. 212(3)(b) (E-05)
E-04.confidence: high for the text; medium for the interpretation of "titik lokasi" in Jakarta
E-04.gaps: DEAL-BREAKER FLAG: IDR 10bn is about CHF 463k per the plan (plan 2, H1; conversion not re-verified here), above the team CHF 200k frame, so an own PT PMA at CHF 200k is not feasible if OSS applies this test (H1 refuted on the text). Open questions for a lawyer (G1): whether DKI Jakarta administrative cities count as kabupaten/kota; whether a second outlet in the same city needs no further IDR 10bn; whether the check is only on the planned value entered in OSS (E-06) or on actual spend; any exemption for restaurants in a mall.

E-06.question: Q2 what counts toward the investment plan and how it is checked
E-06.question_or_metric: For a PMA, OSS validates the planned investment value against the minimum. The plan must cover at least land purchase, buildings, machinery/equipment, other investment (vehicles, office equipment, feasibility study, permits, pre-opening operating costs during construction) and working capital for one turnover (raw materials, wages, building rent, operating costs until ready to operate). The IDR 10bn test excludes land and building (Art. 26).
E-06.value: rencana nilai modal kerja untuk 1 (satu) turnover (working capital for one cycle counts)
E-06.quote_or_snippet: [P2-A1A3-S1] Bagi badan usaha PMA, Sistem OSS melakukan validasi atas rencana nilai investasi || [P2-A1A3-S1] rencana nilai investasi lain-lain, merupakan biaya lainnya yang dikeluarkan || [P2-A1A3-S1] rencana nilai modal kerja untuk 1 (satu) turnover || [P2-A1A3-S1] biaya sewa lahan/gedung || [P2-A1A3-S1] Sumber pembiayaan ... modal sendiri; pinjaman; laba ditanam kembali; agio saham
E-06.notes: If rent, wages and fit-out count, a large part of a single flagship budget could count toward the IDR 10bn, but the threshold itself still stays far above CHF 200k. Run 2 verification (2026-10-17): Art. 364(3)(h) (shortfall against the Art. 26 limit is a sanction ground in supervision) bears on the open question "plan only or actual spend". Fit-out of a leased unit is named in neither Art. 37(4)(b) nor (c) (lawyer question Q4). Audit follow-up (2026-10-17): added Art. 37(5) from opened text, V-P2b. Art. 37(5): financing sources in the OSS entry are own capital, loans, retained profit and share premium (Art. 37(1)(c)); the text does not say a loan-funded plan satisfies the Art. 26 test (lawyer question 4b).
E-06.confidence: medium (text clear; its application to a leased mall unit is interpretation)
E-06.gaps: Whether fit-out of a leased unit and prepaid rent count as "bangunan" (excluded) or as equipment/working capital (counted) is not stated; written lawyer opinion needed (G1). Whether the check applies at planning or against actual spend is not stated in the articles read.

E-07.question: Q2 PMA classed as large enterprise, PT form, any single-outlet relief
E-07.question_or_metric: A PMA is treated as a large enterprise and must follow the minimum investment rule; PMA must be a PT under Indonesian law. The only exceptions listed (wholesale, F&B, construction, industry) all keep the IDR 10bn level but change the counting base; none reduces the amount for a single outlet.

E-12.question: Q3 KBLI 2025 codes for restaurant and cafe
E-12.question_or_metric: OSS and the PP 28/2025 regime use KBLI 2025 (BPS Reg 7/2025). KBLI 56101 = food provision in a fixed building (restaurants, rumah makan, canteens/cafeterias, fast-food restaurants); KBLI 56303 = rumah minum/kafe (mainly drinks, in part or all of a permanent building). KBLI 2020 codes 56102, 56103, 56104, 56109 were merged into KBLI 2025 codes 56101 or 56102.

E-13.question: Q3 leased mall/office unit: location permits and statutory time; fees
E-13.question_or_metric: For a business in a mall, office building or similar shared building whose owner holds KKPR, PL, PBG and SLF, the tenant may use the landlord permits in OSS (lease agreement and landlord NIB plus landlord KKPR/PL/PBG/SLF required). OSS verifies within 5 working days whether KKPR/PL/PBG/SLF are needed. No official fee or total lead time for NIB or Sertifikat Standar was found.

NIB-as-halal-statement applies only to low-risk micro/small businesses.

H-05.question: Q5 may a non-halal outlet or menu operate if it declares it
H-05.question_or_metric: Yes in principle: products made from forbidden (haram) ingredients are exempt from the halal-certificate duty, but must carry a visible non-halal declaration (keterangan tidak halal), easy to see and read and not easily removable. Form and procedure of the declaration are set by a BPJPH head decision. BPJPH FAQ repeats that non-halal products are not banned but must carry the declaration.

H-06.question: Q5 dedicated-facility requirement for halal-certified restaurants (T16 "halal corner")
H-06.question_or_metric: Place and tools (Art. 6(4)) for the halal process must be separated; location separation (Art. 6(3)) applies to slaughter locations only. For the process: from those for non-halal products, including processing, storage, sales and serving. For serving: separate serving facilities and process for halal vs non-halal, serving utensils not used alternately with non-halal, separate cleaning and maintenance facilities, and own storage for halal and non-halal tools. ANALYSIS: the text supports a fully halal kitchen or a clearly separated halal line; a "halal corner" inside a mixed kitchen with shared equipment is not supported by the text.
H-06.value: wajib dipisahkan (place and tools, incl. penyajian; location separation for slaughter only, Art. 6(3))

H-09.question: Q5 LPH inspection fee ceilings (restaurant = service of processing)
H-09.question_or_metric: The LPH (inspection body) fee is set per product type with a ceiling unit cost and mandays by number of products, plus an operational ceiling by enterprise size and local transport and daily allowance. Two Lampiran IV rows could apply to a restaurant: row 17 "Penyediaan makanan dan minuman dengan pengolahan" (unit cost IDR 350,000 micro/small; IDR 3,687,500 medium, large, foreign; mandays by number of products: 0-20 = 4, 21-40 = 5, 41-60 = 6, over 60 = 7) is the category that fits a restaurant or cafe better; row 47 "Jasa Pengolahan" (IDR 350,000 / IDR 5,275,000; mandays 0-50 = 2, 51-100 = 3, 101-200 = 4, over 200 = 5) is a services-category row. The Kepkaban does not state which row the LPH uses for a restaurant (LPH assigns the category, lawyer question Q10). LPH may adjust costs under its own policy (BPJPH calculator note). Total cost is not derived here.

H-11.question: Q5 sanctions for non-compliance (BPJPH statements vs regulation text)
H-11.question_or_metric: For failing the certification duty (Art. 2(1)) the regulation text allows a written warning and withdrawal of the product from circulation; BPJPH (Oct 2024) says only two sanctions: written warning and/or withdrawal including closure of the business for directly served products (restaurants, hotel kitchens, rumah makan, cafes) of medium and large scale. BPJPH (Jun 2026) lists four general sanction types: written warning, administrative fine, certificate revocation, withdrawal. Administrative fine ceiling in the regulation: IDR 2 billion.
H-11.value: peringatan tertulis; penarikan barang dari peredaran (incl. penutupan usaha for restaurants); denda administratif paling banyak dua miliar rupiah
H-11.unit: sanction types; fine ceiling IDR 2bn (not applied to Art. 2(1) per Art. 171(3))
H-11.quote_or_snippet: [P2-A1A3-S9] a. peringatan tertulis; b. denda administratif; c. pencabutan Sertifikat Halal; danf atau d. penarikan barang dari peredaran || [P2-A1A3-S9] (dua miliar rupiah) || [P2-A1A3-S10] penutupan usaha bagi produk yang disajikan secara langsung seperti restoran, dapur hotel, rumah makan, dan kafe untuk skala usaha menengah dan besar || [P2-A1A3-S13] mulai dari peringatan tertulis, denda administratif, pencabutan sertifikat halal, hingga penarikan produk dari peredaran
H-11.notes: Conflict: S10 says only two sanctions; S13 lists four. Run 2 verification (2026-10-17): Art. 170-171 do not contain "penutupan usaha"; that is the BPJPH reading. The fine and revocation do not attach to Art. 2(1) per Art. 171(3)-(4).

H-12.question: Q5 imported Swiss/Italian ingredients and foreign halal certificates
H-12.question_or_metric: For foreign products the halal-certificate duty is to be fixed by the Minister (of Religious Affairs) by 17 Oct 2026 at the latest, after considering mutual recognition of certificates. A foreign halal certificate must be registered with BPJPH (registration fee IDR 800,000 per certificate registration). BPJPH FAQ: imported non-halal products are not banned but need the non-halal declaration; importers need pre-shipment conformity checks (Pemastian Produk Halal). T-10.question: Q6 Indonesia-Switzerland tax treaty: dividends
T-10.question_or_metric: Treaty ceiling on dividends: 10% where the beneficial owner is a company (not a partnership) holding directly at least 25% of the paying company; 15% in all other cases. The DJP rate table shows the same (portfolio 15%, direct participation 10%).

T-10.quote_or_snippet: [P2-TFS-S6] 10% of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly at least 25% of the capital of the company paying the dividends; || [P2-TFS-S6] (b) 15% of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases. || [P2-TFS-S5] Switzerland 10% Yes 15% 10% 33 10% - 10% -

F-02.question_or_metric: STPW is a business licence that every franchise party must hold (franchisor, sub-franchisor, franchisee, sub-franchisee). The franchisor must hold it before making the franchise agreement; the franchisee before starting business. Application is through the OSS system.
F-02.value: STPW mandatory for franchisor (before agreement) and franchisee (before operating)

F-02.notes: Sanctions follow Perizinan Berusaha berbasis risiko rules (Art. 17); revoked franchisors may re-apply only after 5 years (a 5-year bar on re-applying after revocation: the text shows "setelah jangka waktu 5 (lima) tahun sejak penetapan" in two sanction passages; not read in detail, no exact quote).

F-03.question: Q4 STPW for a foreign franchisor and for the local partner of a foreign brand: documents and issuing authority
F-03.question_or_metric: A foreign franchisor must add to its prospectus (a) a business licence document from its home authority, legalised by apostille or by the Indonesian mission, and (b) a statement of continuity of the franchise business from the Indonesian trade attache or mission. The local franchisee of a foreign franchise attaches the foreign franchisor STPW. STPW for foreign and domestic franchisors, sub-franchisors and the franchisee of a foreign franchise is issued by the OSS institution on behalf of the Trade Minister (central, not DKI); only STPW for franchisees of domestic franchises and for sub-franchisees (Penerima Waralaba Lanjutan) are issued on behalf of the Governor of DKI Jakarta (or other regional head).
F-03.value: foreign franchisor: legalised home-country licence + continuity statement; franchisee of foreign brand: STPW issued centrally
F-03.quote_or_snippet: [P2-TFS-S12] Penerima Waralaba berasal dari Waralaba luar negeri dalam mengajukan permohonan STPW sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (21 juga melampirkan STPW Pemberi Waralaba berasal dari luar negeri. || [P2-TFS-S12] surat keterangan keberlangsungan kegiatan usaha Waralaba dari Atase Perdagangan || [P2-TFS-S12] a. STPW Pemberi Waralaba berasal dari luar negeri; || [P2-TFS-S12] e. STPW Penerima Waralaba berasal dari Waralaba luar negeri.
F-03.notes: Permendag 71/2019 Art. 8 earlier required notarised prospectus plus attache letter (superseded in part).
F-03.gaps: Apostille/translation practicalities and processing time for the central STPW not researched. Permendag 25/2025 (F-09) 5-day rule covers regional STPW only.

F-04.question: Q4 Track-record and proven-profit criterion (PP 35/2024)
F-04.question_or_metric: A franchise must be "already profitable": proven by (a) the franchised business having run at least 3 consecutive years, and (b) financial statements for the last 2 years showing profit, audited by a public accountant with an unqualified opinion. Micro and small franchisors are exempt from the audit requirement. This replaces the 5-year experience wording of Permendag 71/2019 (F-05).
F-04.value: 3 consecutive years of operation + 2 years of audited profit
F-04.quote_or_snippet: [P2-TFS-S12] bisnis sudah memberikan keuntungan; || [P2-TFS-S12] berlangsung paling sedikit 3 (tiga) tahun berturut-turut; dan || [P2-TFS-S12] laporan keuangan 2 (dua) tahun terakhir yang menunjukkan adanya keuntungan dan telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik dengan opini wajar tanpa pengecualian.
F-04.notes: Analysis: a young CORSA concept may fail this test at the franchisor level; a trademark/know-how licence outside the franchise definition would avoid it (see F-07), subject to legal advice.
F-04.gaps: Whether the franchised business must have run in Indonesia or may be proven abroad (the foreign-franchisor route in F-03 suggests home-country evidence) is not stated in the text read; whether CORSA (a young concept, Swiss-Italian) meets 3 years + 2 audited profitable years is an open fact about the brand, not researched here.

F-05.question: Q4 Permendag 71/2019: 5-year experience requirement (conflict with PP 35/2024)
F-05.question_or_metric: CONFLICT STORED (rule e): Permendag 71/2019 Art. 2(3) says the profit criterion is met when the franchisor has at least 5 years of experience and a business know-how, shown by the business surviving and growing profitably. JDIH Kemendag still lists the Permendag as Berlaku, and none of the later instruments read repeals it, but PP 35/2024 Art. 4(5) now states 3 years plus 2 audited profitable years. F-06.question: Q4 Local-goods (domestic product) obligation
F-06.question_or_metric: PP 35/2024 requires franchisors and franchisees to "prioritise" (mengutamakan) domestic goods/services, for franchisees only as far as they meet the franchisor written quality standards; franchisors must cooperate with local MSMEs as suppliers and give local MSMEs the chance to become franchisees; franchise operators must also prioritise domestic raw-material processing. The text states no percentage quota and no ban on imports.
F-06.value: prioritise domestic goods/services; no percentage quota in Art. 26-27
F-06.quote_or_snippet: [P2-TFS-S12] mengutamakan penggunaan barang dan/atau jasa hasil produksi dalam negeri sepanjang memenuhi standar mutu barang dan/atau jasa yang ditetapkan secara tertulis oleh Pemberi Waralaba || [P2-TFS-S12] mengutamakan pengolahan bahan baku di dalam negeri. || [P2-TFS-S13] mengutamakan penggunaan barang dan/atau jasa hasil produksi dalam negeri sepanjang memenuhi standar mutu barang dan/atau jasa yang ditetapkan secara tertulis oleh Pemberi Waralaba || [P2-TFS-S12] Pasal 3 huruf b sampai dengan huruf d
F-06.notes: Practical fact: imported Italian ingredients are not banned; the duty is to give domestic supply a priority subject to quality. Audit follow-up (2026-10-17): added Art. 3(b)-(d) from opened text, V-P2b. PP 35/2024 Art. 3(b) domestic franchisor, (c) sub-franchisor of a foreign franchise, (d) sub-franchisor of a domestic franchise. Art. 26(1), (3), (5) bind Art. 3(b)-(d); Art. 26(2), (4) bind Art. 3(e)-(h); (2) is conditional on the franchisor's written quality standards, (4) and (5) on the franchisor's requirements.
F-06.amendment_check: Hukumonline reports that the Permendag 71/2019 removed the earlier percentage limit; not opened.
F-06.confidence: high for the wording; the legal force of "mengutamakan" (priority vs mandate) is analysis
F-06.gaps: No sanction specific to Art. 26 found in the text read; Art. 26(6) refers to implementing rules ("berdasarkan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan"), which were not searched (TKDN rules).

F-07.question: Q4 Do these rules apply to a foreign brand licensing a local partner
F-07.question_or_metric: Yes, if the arrangement is a "Waralaba" (a right to use a business system on terms of a franchise agreement): the PP names foreign franchisors (Pemberi Waralaba berasal dari luar negeri) and franchisees of foreign franchises as regulated parties, so the STPW, criteria, local-supplier and agreement rules apply to a Swiss brand granting a local partner rights to operate CORSA. Whether a pure trademark licence without a business system and support falls outside the definition is not settled by the text read (analysis: open lawyer question).
F-07.value: applies to foreign franchisor and to the local franchisee of a foreign franchise

Pemberi Waralaba berasal dari luar negeri; || [P2-TFS-S12] e. Penerima Waralaba berasal dari Waralaba luar negeri;
F-07.notes: Not a PT PMA question: franchise to a local licensee does not trigger the PT PMA investment threshold (E-04), the STPW and franchise criteria instead.

F-09.question: Q4 2025 amendment: Permendag 25/2025 on STPW issuance by regional governments
F-09.question_or_metric: Permendag 25/2025 (30 Jun 2025) sets the procedure for regional governments (incl. the DKI Governor) to issue STPW: verification and issuance within at most 5 working days, and if not issued in time the application receipt serves as provisional proof of franchise business until the STPW is issued. STPW Penerima Waralaba berasal dari Waralaba dalam negeri; || [P2-TFS-S14] Ditetapkan di Jakarta pada tanggal 30 Juni 2025

ENV-012.question: Jakarta plastic-bag ban: who is bound and what is allowed?
ENV-012.question_or_metric: Pergub DKI 142/2019 (official JDIH Jakarta text): managers of shopping centres, supermarkets/minimarkets and traditional markets must use reusable "eco-friendly" bags and may not use single-use plastic shopping bags (Art. 5); shopping-centre managers must impose this on every tenant (Art. 6(1)(a)-(b)); every tenant (pelaku usaha) must not provide single-use plastic shopping bags at its premises and must sell reusable bags, not free, near the till (Art. 6(2)(a)-(b)); supermarkets must sell reusable bags near the till (Art. 9(1)(b)); single-use plastic packaging bags remain allowed for unwrapped food until a greener alternative exists (Art. 7).
ENV-012.quote_or_snippet: Pengelola Pusat Perbelanjaan, Toko Swalayan, dan Pasar Rakyat wajib menggunakan Kantong Belanja Ramah Lingkungan. || Pelaku Usaha di Pusat Perbelanjaan dapat menyediakan Kantong Kemasan Plastik Sekali Pakai. (2) ... hanya dapat digunakan untuk mewadahi bahan Pangan yang belum terselubung kemasan apapun.
ENV-012.notes: Interpretation: a mall-based cafe is bound through the mall manager. Food-and-drink takeaway bags/cups are not addressed in the opened articles. Audit follow-up (2026-10-17): upgraded from tier-3 Pasal.id relay to the official JDIH Jakarta full text (https://jdih.jakarta.go.id/link/download-fulltext/3851, opened 2026-10-17, article numbers and quotes checked against the PDF). Art. 6(2) (tenant duties) added; the earlier wording that only managers are bound is incomplete. Sale of reusable bags: "tidak gratis" (not free).
ENV-012.gaps: Whether a stand-alone street cafe outside a mall is bound is not clear from the articles (they bind mall, supermarket and market managers; Art. 9(2) on stand-alone supermarkets read only in part). Takeaway cups and straws are not addressed.

ENV-013.question: Jakarta plastic-bag ban: sanctions, effective date and in-force status
ENV-013.question_or_metric: Official JDIH Jakarta text: sanctions on managers are written warning, forced payment (uang paksa), licence suspension, licence revocation (Art. 22(2)); the forced payment is at least IDR 5,000,000 and at most IDR 25,000,000 (Art. 24(1)); tenants (pelaku usaha) who knowingly allow single-use plastic shopping bags receive a written warning from the Environment Agency (Art. 29); the Pergub applies 6 months after promulgation (Art. 30), derived start about 30 June 2020; JDIH record status "Berlaku".
ENV-013.unit: status per JDIH Jakarta record 3851; applies 6 months after 2019-12-31 (BD Prov DKI 2019 No. 64003)
ENV-013.quote_or_snippet: Peraturan Gubernur ini mulai berlaku 6 (enam) bulan terhitung sejak tanggal diundangkan. || a. teguran tertulis; b. uang paksa; c. pembekuan izin; dan/atau d. pencabutan izin. || uang paksa paling sedikit Rp5.000.000,- ... dan paling banyak Rp25.000.000,- || dikenakan sanksi administratif berupa teguran tertulis.
ENV-013.notes: Sanctions fall on the manager, with a licence sanction issued by the DPMPTSP. Audit follow-up (2026-10-17): upgraded to tier 1 (JDIH Jakarta). Added Art. 24 (forced payment IDR 5m to 25m) and Art. 29 (tenant written warning); the earlier note "sanctions fall on the manager" was incomplete: a tenant can itself be warned. Licence sanctions (Art. 22(5)) are issued by DPMPTSP to the holder of the operating licence.

P4W2b-19.value: qualitative: positive and significant effect on customer trust (both restaurants); no rating threshold or reading share reported

P4W2b-19.quote_or_snippet: data collected from 400 respondents who have visited the selected restaurants and interacted with Google Maps ratings and reviews. The results reveal that Google Maps ratings and reviews have a positive and significant effect on customer trust in both restaurants.

Selection bias: only people who used Google Maps reviews. No finding on a minimum star rating or on the share who read reviews before visiting (gap). Run 2 verification (2026-10-17): full text confirms non-probability purposive sampling, respondents aged 17+, 21-25 = 178 (44.5%).
